alex: Quick question — I'm about to merge a PR that flips the default for `experimental-encoder` to `off` at the route level, but we want dev teams to be able to opt in via a model-level override. Which precedence rule applies at runtime? If a model-level `override` exists, does it always win over the route default? Need to unblock PR 4753, pinging @maya @jamal :wave:
maya: Short answer: model-level overrides were explicit-hotfixes last sprint so they get higher precedence only if the override metadata sets `priority: elevated`. Otherwise route value stands. We added that because we wanted safe defaults + emergency fixes.
jamal: To be explicit: resolution order is based on (1) explicit override w/ priority, (2) scoped values by specificity (route > project > org), (3) global default. Implementation detail: `resolveFlag` picks the highest-priority candidate; if two candidates have same priority, we choose the most specific scope.
sasha: Also note: canary audiences are checked after resolution. So even if the resolved value is `on` due to a model override, the canary% gating still applies unless the override includes `bypass_canary: true`. We discourage bypasses except for emergency patches.
deploy-bot: :information_source: Canary rollout started for route `/recommend` at 2% for experiment `encoder-canary` (canary id: c-20250315-7). Monitor: https://console.redwood/inference/canaries/c-20250315-7
clare: For docs brevity, we have this rule: `explicitOverride > route > project > org > default`, but with the caveat that override only wins if `override.priority >= elevated_threshold`. Also there is a `bypass_canary` flag that requires `is_emergency=true` in rollout metadata and manual approval. I'll paste a short snippet in the PR.
alex: Got it. So to safely unblock my PR I'll: leave route default `off`, allow model teams to add an override (without `bypass_canary`), and require approval for any override that sets `bypass_canary`. Who should be the approver for those?
maya: Approvals should be product owner + infra oncall. We decided that in the rollout playbook, cc @clare for infra automation.
clare: I'll add a CI lint check in the flag validation step to reject `bypass_canary:true` unless the PR includes `approved_by: ["product", "infra"]`. I'll also patch the docs with the tiny flow diagram.
jamal: For the code change you mentioned: I pushed a tiny change in the flag service to make precedence explicit. Tests added. Key snippet: ```js
// choose override if it exists and has sufficient priority
if (override && override.priority >= scope.priority) return override.value;
// otherwise fall back to the most specific scoped value
return pickMostSpecific(scopeCandidates);
```
alex: Perfect. I'll link PR 4753 here and wait for clare's CI rule before merging. Thanks everyone :pray:
clare: Will do the lint rule after standup (ETA ~1.5h). I'll post a follow-up when it's live.
sasha: One operational note — add telemetry tags `flag_source` and `resolved_by` to the logs so we can trace when model overrides are used in production. Minimal overhead and helpful for debugging.
alex: Good call, adding a TODO to the PR. If anyone sees anything else that must block merge speak now, otherwise I'll go ahead once CI passes. :thumbsup:
